metric: Final proof size for a 1,000-step computation (bytes, log scale). Folding-based IVC holds constant regardless of N; batch STARKs and separate SNARK proofs grow with depth.

schemes.label: Groth16 × N
schemes.note: One Groth16 proof per step. Proof = 3 bn254 group elements = exactly 192 bytes, so N=1000 separate proofs = 192 KB. Verifier must check N proofs; no aggregation without extra cost.

schemes.label: STARK full trace
schemes.note: Full-trace FRI-STARK over all N steps. Proof grows as O(log²N × λ) where λ is security parameter. SP1 / RISC Zero STARKs run 100–500 KB in practice; on-chain verification ~327k gas (Zinnia benchmark, ePrint 2025/572).

schemes.label: Recursive Groth16
schemes.note: Each recursion step wraps the prior Groth16 verifier in a new circuit. Proof stays constant (~2 KB) but the verifier circuit costs ~150k R1CS constraints per step — 10× more expensive than Nova's folding step.

schemes.label: Nova IVC
schemes.note: Folds N steps into one constant-size relaxed R1CS accumulator. SHA-256 benchmark: 53 ms/step at 55k constraints (microsoft/Nova). Recursion overhead: ~15k constraints — 10× less than SNARK-based IVC. Final Spartan-compressed proof is ~7,400× smaller than the uncompressed IVC state.

schemes.label: HyperNova IVC
schemes.note: Extends Nova to CCS (Customizable Constraint Systems), simultaneously generalizing R1CS, Plonkish, and AIR. Prover cost per fold: one MSM of size = number of witnesses (optimal for MSM-based schemes). Handles transformer's mixed linear + nonlinear ops in one constraint framework.

schemes.label: NANOZK (GPT-2, 12 layers)
schemes.note: Layerwise ZK proofs for verifiable LLM inference. GPT-2 scale: 43s proving, 6.9 KB proof, 23ms verification — constant in hidden dimension. Lookup table approximations for softmax, GELU, LayerNorm with zero measurable accuracy loss. 52× speedup over EZKL.
